For nineteen months there were two Italies. Both claimed to be the real one, both had an Italian army, and they fought each other.

The Italian Civil War, 1943-1945 — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Panel one: 8 September 1943, the day the armistice with the Allies was announced. Within hours German forces launched Operation Achse — disarming their own ally, seizing the peninsula, and interning several hundred thousand Italian soldiers.

2/ The king and the government fled south to Brindisi. Mussolini, arrested in July, was sprung from a hotel on the Gran Sasso by German paratroopers on 12 September and installed at the head of a new state proclaimed later that month.

3/ That state — the Italian Social Republic, red on the map — took its informal name from Salò, the small town on Lake Garda where several ministries sat. It was a German client, but it raised its own divisions and its own police.

4/ Panel two, 12 October 1943. The Allies had landed at Salerno and taken Naples; the south is dark. The day after this snapshot, the Kingdom of Italy declared war on Germany and became an Allied co-belligerent. Italian troops now faced Italian troops.

5/ Panel three, 8 July 1944. Rome fell on 4 June and the line has jumped north of it — then stalled on the Gothic Line across the Apennines for a brutal winter. Look at how little moves between panels two and three: ten months for central Italy.

6/ Behind the front, a second war. Partisan brigades grew into a force of well over a hundred thousand, and German and RSI units answered with reprisals against civilians — Sant'Anna di Stazzema, Marzabotto, the Ardeatine Caves in Rome.

7/ Panel four, 29 April 1945: the day German forces in Italy signed their surrender at Caserta. Mussolini had been caught and shot by partisans the day before, near Lake Como, while trying to reach Switzerland.

8/ For decades Italy preferred to call this the Liberation. Calling it a civil war only became mainstream after historian Claudio Pavone made the case in 1991 — because it meant admitting how many Italians chose the other side.
